newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence minister fears extreme instability.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister fears extreme instability.

text.p: Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Tuesday Russia's political and economic instability had become "extreme" and poor military readiness could have dire consequences, Interfax news agency said.
The agency also quoted Rodionov, who has been campaigning for better funding for the army, as telling top generals the lack of funding could lead to dire consequences.
"The armed forces have reached a borderline, beyond which any further fall in their combat readiness may lead to 'unpredictable, catastrophic consequences'," Interfax said.
"According to his words, political and economic instability in Russia have become 'extreme'," the agency said.
Rodionov was speaking at a meeting of Russia's top brass which was due to discuss the results of combat training in 1996.

The meeting, closed to foreign media, was attended by Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and Russia's top security officials. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was scheduled to meet generals later on Tuesday.
Rodionov has been ringing alarm bells about the state of affairs in the military to try to get more funding for the armed forces this year and in the 1997 budget.
A meeting of Russia's advisory Defence Council said on Monday the government had failed to settle its wages arrears to the military, the liberal Sevodnya newspaper said on Tuesday.
Interfax also quoted Rodionov as saying the global strategic and military situation could provoke military conflicts which would threaten Russia's security. He gave no details.
RIA news agency quoted Rodionov as saying that 1996 was the most difficult year for the armed forces since the start of market reforms in 1992.
